name: velcurve reshapes a note on's velocity and leaves a release alone
about: velcurve puts a note on's velocity through a table of points, as curve does a CC, then clamps to 1..127 so a note on never becomes a release.
notes: points (0,0) (40,10) (100,120). The same interpolation and rounding as curve, on a note on with v > 0 only, then clamped to 1..127.
t 0: v 1, segment 0..40: 0 + 1 * 10 / 40 = 0.25, rounds to 0 and CLAMPS UP to 1 = 01. Without the clamp it would be 90 3C 00, a release.
t 1: v 10 (0A): 10 * 10 / 40 = 2.5, a TIE, away from zero 3 = 03. Truncating gives 2, ties to even gives 2.
t 4: v 100 (64) is the last point: 120 = 78.
t 5: v 127 (7F) is above the last point and CLAMPS to its out, 120 = 78, not 127.
NEGATIVE CONTROL t 6: a note off with release velocity 64 (80 3C 40) passes unchanged. Curved it would read 80 3C 36, since 10 + 24 * 110 / 60 = 54.
NEGATIVE CONTROL t 7: 90 3D 00 is a release and passes unchanged. Curved and clamped it would become 90 3D 01, a note on that never ends.
NEGATIVE CONTROL t 8: a CC value is not a velocity, B0 07 0A passes unchanged.
NEGATIVE CONTROL t 9: a poly touch carries a pressure, not a velocity, A0 3C 0A passes unchanged.
NEGATIVE CONTROL: l2 has two points with the same input (0 and 0) and is refused bad-args. Inputs must rise strictly.
NEGATIVE CONTROL: l3 has no points at all and is refused bad-args.
